methods.label: Measure bench space
methods.sourceMethod: Uses the fractional bench-length model in LIVE and AoPS Solution 2, with the coprimality argument supplied explicitly to establish minimality. The 77-person construction also appears in AoPS Solution 1.

annotationRationale: The central step is imposing integer restrictions on the equation for occupied bench length. Fraction addition and coprimality support the divisibility argument.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Number Theory is appropriate. No area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The statement, choices and key agree: the minimum is 18, choice B. No figure or grading contradiction is present.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: No additional route is needed. The references' LCM and fractional-length arguments use the same underlying divisibility restriction.
review.annotationCheck: Integer solutions are the central assessment; fraction addition and coprimality are appropriate supporting concepts.
review.areaCheck: Number Theory is appropriate. No area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The length equation gives 77N=18P. Since gcd(77,18)=1, all positive solutions have P=77t and N=18t. Taking t=1 constructs a full seating arrangement and proves the minimum is 18.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Both cited references support this model. The source-informed-original classification correctly identifies nonofficial third-party influence. The prose is independently developed, and the explicit prime-divisibility argument supplies the references' missing minimality justification.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The fractional-space model is motivated, and the explanation connects integrality, divisibility, minimality and an attainable arrangement clearly.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All three IDs fit: the integer-equation node captures the decisive restriction, cnm_p173 supports common-denominator addition, and cnm_p158 supports the coprimality check.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native fraction-addition and GCF links support the procedures used. Only coprimality is exercised from the GCF topic. The central integer-equation node has no supplied CN alignment.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 5.NF.A.1 and the modeling component of 5.NF.A.2 overlap; benchmark estimation is absent. 6.NS.B.4 contributes only its GCF component. The tenths/hundredths restriction of 4.NF.C.5 does not directly cover denominators 7 and 11. No US alignment is supplied for integer equations.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The assessed/support roles are appropriate. The derivation directly exercises integrality restrictions and explains why the least admissible positive solution works.
